rule_name: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Interiority of non-POV characters)
quote: starting with the one he thinks is strongest
why: attributes Kavi's internal ranking of his own objections as narrated fact, which is interiority of a non-POV character
suggestion: starting with the objection he lists first and working down

rule_name: Subordinate Instead of Chaining With "And" / "Then"
quote: and then a third time, and then she goes down two flights at a run and comes into the dining hall loud
why: three actions of very different weight (a reread, a stair run, a loud entrance) are coordinated with repeated "and then" instead of being ranked by subordination
suggestion: and then a third time, before running down two flights and coming into the dining hall loud

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: That's the last of it.
why: a near-variant of the listed reflexive scene-closer "that's the end of it," adding nothing after "That's it" already lands the point
suggestion: cut it, leaving "That's it. I am never doing either of those again as long as I live."

rule_name: Dialogue Tag Clutter, Let Action Beats Carry Tone
quote: Ruth says, without looking up from her book,
why: loads the dialogue tag with a prepositional aside about circumstance instead of giving the physical detail its own beat
suggestion: Ruth doesn't look up from her book. "You were good at dance," she says, "which is why you liked it, Sam..."

rule_name: The "Nobody" Construction, Don't Normalise by Reporting an Absent Reaction
quote: Ruth turns a page without commenting on any of it
why: reports a named bystander's absent reaction as evidence Chloe's outburst is unremarkable, the same device the rule bans for crowds applied to one character
suggestion: Ruth turns a page and licks her thumb for the next one

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: She hears the four tones as four different people saying one word
why: routes the auditory distinction through the filter verb "hears" instead of rendering the sound itself
suggestion: The four tones sound like four different people saying one word

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: so she knows they are different
why: "knows" filters the conclusion instead of showing the reader the evidence for it
suggestion: four different people, one word, though she can't make the difference happen in her own mouth

rule_name: Telling After Showing, Don't Explain the Image You Just Rendered
quote: Hearing it is worse than not hearing it, and that turns out to be the point.
why: explains the significance of the image (reading aloud into the machine, hearing herself back) immediately after the image already showed it
suggestion: cut the sentence and end the beat on "plays it back, and hears it."

rule_name: Vague Abstractions, Replace "Something," "Nothing," "The Whole Thing"
quote: there is nothing left of it
why: near-verbatim reuse of the rule's own banned example ("nothing left in the worksheet to find out"), a placeholder standing in for a specific image
suggestion: until the number is down to its last decimal

rule_name: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Superlatives in narration)
quote: Chloe likes it more than she has liked anything since the fractions
why: a narrator ranking of her own feelings rather than a rendered fact; superlatives are only sanctioned in dialogue
suggestion: Chloe brings a worksheet to dinner and won't put it down until pudding

rule_name: The Predictable Correction Pattern, Vary the Beat You've Trained the Reader to Expect
quote: Glassware, reagent, or you, and the fix is the same fix either way.
why: a third instance in this chapter of the confident-question then authority-correction-with-mechanism beat (after the office scene and Mrs. Sun), which starts to read as a predictable shape
suggestion: "Water," he says, and turns back to his desk, leaving her to work out where from

rule_name: The Predictable Correction Pattern, Vary the Beat You've Trained the Reader to Expect
quote: He's going to keep asking. That's the room you'll be in, and this is that room with the temperature turned down.
why: a fourth instance of the same correction-then-mechanism beat inside one chapter
suggestion: cut the explanation and let the drill continue uncommented: "He's going to keep asking. Count out loud."

rule_name: Invented similes versus inherited similes
quote: geometry with cloth in it
why: a newly built, writerly comparison delivered by the narrator rather than a character, and not a stock or inherited figure
suggestion: Textiles turns out to mean measuring, drafting patterns onto brown paper, and cutting

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: builds the whole thing over
why: "the whole thing" is the rule's own listed crutch phrase, used here as filler instead of naming what she rebuilt
suggestion: builds the shirt over from the armhole out

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: produces a diagram of the whole thing
why: a second instance of the listed crutch phrase "the whole thing"
suggestion: produces a diagram of the tank, arrows and all

rule_name: Ration a Character's Verbal Tic to the Moments It Characterises
quote: Kavi watches the tank for eleven days
why: the exact-duration habit is attached to Kavi's scene rather than Chloe's, the narration defaulting to precise counting regardless of whose moment it is
suggestion: Kavi watches the tank for what turns out to be most of October

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: a while back
why: "for a while"/"a while" is listed as a universal duration marker used as filler regardless of what kind of moment is being timed
suggestion: he stopped listening around the second sentence

rule_name: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Symmetry / mirrored halves)
quote: Nothing has happened between her and either one of them, and nothing is going to.
why: two clauses built from the identical "nothing... nothing" shape restate the same claim rather than adding to it
suggestion: Nothing has happened between her and either one of them, and she isn't waiting for it to

rule_name: Reification and the grep test
quote: Both things sit there next to each other and stay exactly where they are.
why: hands the abstract facts ("both things") physical verbs, sit and stay, as if they were objects that could be placed and left, exactly the pattern the grep test targets
suggestion: She dislikes him, and she'd take him again tomorrow, and neither fact changes the other

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: sits on the mat a while saying he is fine
why: another instance of "a while" as a vague universal duration marker rather than a real one
suggestion: sits on the mat for a count of ten, saying he is fine

rule_name: Subordinate Instead of Chaining With "And" / "Then"
quote: and she tells him, and the answer turns out to be about where you put your left foot before you start
why: chains the telling and the answer with flat "and" coordination, giving them equal weight instead of subordinating the trivial to the consequential
suggestion: then goes and asks her how she did it. The answer turns out to be about where you put your left foot before you start

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: Left foot's the whole thing.
why: a third instance of the listed crutch phrase "the whole thing" used as filler emphasis
suggestion: Left foot's what does it.

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: She was right about the left foot.
why: a bare verdict-of-correctness sentence from the banned "you're right" family that supplies no new fact beyond confirming she was correct
suggestion: Left foot first, same as she said

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: Chloe knows the name of every horse in the place
why: routes her accumulated competence through the filter verb "knows" instead of rendering it directly
suggestion: Chloe can call every horse in the place by name

rule_name: The Predictable Correction Pattern, Vary the Beat You've Trained the Reader to Expect
quote: Straight in front is the one place they can't, and nobody believes me when I say it, so watch.
why: a fifth instance in the chapter of a figure delivering the confident-correction-then-mechanism beat
suggestion: cut "and nobody believes me when I say it, so watch" and let the horse's head swinging round stand as the proof

rule_name: Vague Abstractions, Replace "Something," "Nothing," "The Whole Thing"
quote: it is not the thing either
why: "the thing" is a vague placeholder standing in for whatever feeling isn't jealousy, unnamed instead of shown
suggestion: it is not that she wants what Priya has, either

rule_name: Vague Abstractions, Replace "Something," "Nothing," "The Whole Thing"
quote: in a way she cannot name
why: a vague-abstraction hedge that gestures at a feeling instead of giving a concrete image for it
suggestion: restful enough that she wants a second film, so they watch one

rule_name: The Predictable Correction Pattern, Vary the Beat You've Trained the Reader to Expect
quote: There isn't a run, that's why I said six.
why: a sixth instance of the confident-mistake/correction/mechanism beat recurring in one chapter (office, Mrs. Sun, Vasquez, first aid, Priya, now her mother)
suggestion: "There isn't a run." Her mother moves a peg.

rule_name: Subordinate Instead of Chaining With "And" / "Then"
quote: and then the fifth, and her mother says a word she does not usually say in front of her and deals again, and they play until the pool lights go off at eleven
why: four clauses of unequal weight are chained flatly with "and," burying the more consequential beat (her mother swearing) among the trivial ones
suggestion: then the fifth, at which her mother says a word she doesn't usually say in front of her before dealing again; they play until the pool lights go off at eleven

rule_name: The trailing clause
quote: which he lets her do
why: a comma-trailing clause after a complete sentence that only comments on the preceding action instead of adding a new fact
suggestion: cut it: "Chloe reads over his shoulder until she stops on the second paragraph."

rule_name: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Em dashes)
quote: othing there at all, which is the entire—" Chloe stops, beca
why: em dash; the ban applies everywhere, dialogue included
suggestion: replace with a comma or a short hyphen
